text:
marta: Heads up — saw an odd spike in KMS permission grants tied to BYOK customers in eu-west1 during last night's provisioning job.
leo: can you paste the log lines? which principal is doing the calls?
marta: looks like a deploy job principal. excerpt: 
```
2026-03-20T22:03:11Z principal=redwood-deploy-batcher@infra svc=keymanager.action=ListKeys resource=projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu-west1
2026-03-20T22:03:12Z principal=redwood-deploy-batcher@infra svc=keymanager.action=GetKeyMetadata resource=projects/redwood-prod/locations/eu-west1/keyRings/byok-kr/cryptoKeys/customer-abc
```
anya: ew, that principal shouldn't have ListKeys for customer key rings. did we recently change a role in infra-project?
samir: I pushed a patch yesterday that consolidated some service accounts into `roles/redwood.deployer` — probable scope expansion. rolling back check in progress.
infra-bot: deploy 6731 started by samir at 2026-03-20T21:58:00Z; changes: infra/iam/service-account-roles.yaml
leo: important: for BYOK customers we must never grant cross-tenant `viewer`-like access to deployer SA. that violates custody boundaries.
reena: are the calls just metadata/listing or were there crypto ops?
marta: only ListKeys and GetKeyMetadata in logs. no Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign calls.
security-oncall: still treat as high — it's a principle-of-least-privilege regression + logging gap. do we have continuous HSM import/provisioning audit forwarded to SIEM?
anya: we discovered a gap: HSM import events from the on-prem side weren't forwarded due to a broken forwarder between 21:30 and 04:00 UTC. so correlated events might be missing for ~6.5h.
leo: ok immediate steps: 1) revoke `roles/redwood.deployer` from `redwood-deploy-batcher` in eu-west1; 2) rollback IAM change; 3) re-run log forwarder replay (if possible) and mark missing window; 4) notify affected customers and compliance. anyone object?
samir: +1, rolling back now. I'll also run `gcloud logging read` and export results to forensics bucket.
reena: note for BYOK customers we can't rotate their keys without explicit consent. mitigation is RBAC revert + audit + suggest customer-initiated rewrap if they want to be safe. also consider temporary denylist for deployer SA on customer keyrings.
marta: agree on denylist. can we script a KMS resource-level IAM deny for known BYOK keyRings?
leo: yes — implement a conditional deny via organization policy or set a deny IAM binding on the specific key rings. add to playbook.
security-oncall: escalation checklist: document timeline, collect logs (including replays), inform SOC, prepare customer notification template referencing potential exposure to metadata only (no crypto ops). legal should review wording.
anya: who will own customer comms? product-comms or account?
reena: account execs should own notification. security will supply the template + evidence.
infra-bot: rollback commit 9a3f applied by samir at 2026-03-20T22:25:42Z; status=success
leo: followups (post-mortem actions): - add CI gate preventing deployer role from being granted on keyRing resources; - increase retention/replication for HSM import logs to avoid forwarder single-point-of-failure; - add an alert when non-owner principals call ListKeys on BYOK keyRings.
samir: capturing those as issues now. will also add automated SIEM reingestion job for the missing window.
marta: timeline note: first anomalous ListKeys 22:03, rollback 22:25, forwarder outage 21:30-04:00.
leo: confirm last point: last_message_ts should include when we finish collection? keep it open until logs reingested.
security-oncall: I'll open an incident ticket and set priority P2. will ping legal and account teams.
reena: thanks team. after we finish, we need to update the BYOK onboarding checklist: require explicit deny bindings for all infra/automation SAs and annual RBAC review.
marta: filing a short postmortem thread after logs are in. :thumbsup:
leo: nice catch marta.
anya: noted.
security-oncall: closing interim; will update here when SIEM replay completes.
